title: Factor source-node × target-node edge-function codes
hypothesis: Factorizing edge-function identity into source and target node codes reconstructs heldout edge functions with fewer bytes than independent edge transforms and improves on native low-rank GS-KAN coefficients.

world.teacher: edge affine scale is source_code*target_code; edge shift is source_bias+target_bias
world.heldout: eight source-target pairs withheld from error scoring; codes remain stored

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after native low-rank factor alias or storage/quality gate miss.

controls: native rank-2 GS-KAN edge coefficient matrix
success_gate: heldout nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer bytes than independent edges and strict quality/byte gain over native rank-2 coefficient matrix.
failure_gate: FAIL if native coefficient factorization matches Mirror or storage/quality gate misses.
boundaries: Synthetic analytic scalar edge functions only; no KAN model claim.
Heldout combinations use stored source/target codes; no unseen-node inference test.
No fresh run after exact native factor alias or gate failure.
